doc.name: A — e bike catalogue, paper craft set, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: step-through e-bike
Category: e bike
Shot programme: paper craft set
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing an e bike capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the extreme wide set in a paper craft set treatment.

SUBJECT. A step-through e-bike. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Wide frame with the product small in a large, deliberately empty set. Shoot on a 28mm at f/5.6, framing for dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a book light bounce producing an extremely soft wrap. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
